files.html: //! examples/audio_scale_star - the notes and the chords of the major scale, drawn around a circle in thirds. //! //! The seven notes of C major sit on a circle, clockwise from the top, in the order 1 3 5 7 2 4 6: each note a third //! above the one before it. A third is two steps of the scale, and a chord of the scale - a triad - is a note with //! the third and the fifth above it, so on this circle every chord is three neighbours: its root, its third and its //! fifth. C major (I) is 1 3 5; D minor (ii) is 2 4 6; and so on round the circle. //! //! 1 C each chord is drawn beside the middle of its three notes, its third: //! 6 A 3 E the major chords (I, IV, V) outside the circle, the minor ones (ii, iii, vi) //! and the diminished one (vii) inside //! 4 F 5 G //! lines lead from a chord to its notes, one style for each role: //! 2 D 7 B root a solid line ending in an arrowhead //! third a zigzag //! fifth a dashed line //! //! A major chord - I, IV, V - is a square, and so is each note whose own chord is major - 1, 4, 5; the minor chords //! - ii, iii, vi - and the diminished vii are circles, as are the notes 2, 3, 6 and 7: the major side and the minor //! side of the scale can be told apart at a glance. Each chord but vii fills the triangles between it, its root and its //! third, and between it, its third and its fifth, faintly with its color - the first less faintly than the second. //! Everything is placed from the window's size, so the drawing fills a phone held either way. //! //! It plays. The digits 1 to 7 - on the top row or the keypad - and a press on a note play that note while held; a //! press on a chord plays its three notes while held, and sliding to another note or chord while pressed plays that //! one instead. What sounds is lit: a note while it sounds, and a chord while all three of its notes do - so that 1, 3 //! and 5 held on the keyboard light the chord I as a press on I does. The notes are Shepard tones //! (`z.mixer.shepard_instrument`): each note sounds in every octave at once under one fixed bell, so the notes differ //! in pitch class and not in height, and a scale played round the circle neither rises nor falls. const std = @import("std"); const Allocator = std.mem.Allocator; const bufPrint = std.fmt.bufPrint; const indexOfScalar = std.mem.indexOfScalar; const z = @import("zimr"); const zm = @import("zm"); const Color = zm.Color; const Vec2 = zm.Vec2; const float = zm.float; const sinTurns = zm.sinTurns; const cosTurns = zm.cosTurns; const length = zm.length; const assert = zm.assert; const inf = zm.inf; const splat2 = zm.splat2; const atkinson_mono_ttf = @embedFile("atkinson_mono_ttf"); const background: Color = .{ .r = 16, .g = 17, .b = 22, .a = 255 }; const text_color: Color = .{ .r = 235, .g = 235, .b = 240, .a = 255 }; const dim_text_color: Color = .{ .r = 150, .g = 156, .b = 170, .a = 255 }; const circle_path_color: Color = .{ .r = 70, .g = 74, .b = 90, .a = 255 }; const outline_color: Color = .{ .r = 225, .g = 228, .b = 236, .a = 255 }; /// Text on a lit note or chord, which is filled with its full color: dark, since some of the colors are light. const lit_text_color: Color = .{ .r = 16, .g = 17, .b = 22, .a = 255 }; /// Each degree's color, as a rainbow keyboard colors its white keys from C: red, orange, yellow, green, cyan, blue, /// violet. A note is filled with its color, dimmed until it sounds; a chord takes its root's color. const degree_colors = [7]Color{ .rgbHex(0xF52A2A), .rgbHex(0xFFA514), .rgbHex(0xFFF200), .rgbHex(0x18E018), .rgbHex(0x18E6F0), .rgbHex(0x1464FF), .rgbHex(0xA83CF0), }; /// How far toward the background a color is drawn while its note or chord is silent: lit, it is drawn whole. const resting_dimming: f32 = 0.45; /// How far toward the background a chord's triangles are drawn (`drawChordTriangles`): faint while the chord is /// silent, a little less faint while it sounds. const TriangleDimming = struct { resting: f32, lit: f32, }; /// The triangle between the root and the third is the more opaque of a chord's two: the third is what makes a chord /// major or minor. The one between the third and the fifth is fainter. const root_third_dimming: TriangleDimming = .{ .resting = 0.8, .lit = 0.6 }; const third_fifth_dimming: TriangleDimming = .{ .resting = 0.9, .lit = 0.76 }; /// A degree's color, whole while it sounds and dimmed while it does not. fn colorOfDegree(degree: u8, is_lit: bool) Color { const whole_color: Color = degree_colors[degree - 1]; return if (is_lit) whole_color else whole_color.lerp(background, resting_dimming); } // ---- The scale ---- /// A note of the major scale: its degree, from 1 (the tonic) to 7, and its names - the letter of C major and the /// solfege syllable. const ScaleNote = struct { degree: u8, letter: []const u8, solfege: []const u8, }; /// The seven notes of C major, by degree. const scale_notes = [7]ScaleNote{ .{ .degree = 1, .letter = "C", .solfege = "do" }, .{ .degree = 2, .letter = "D", .solfege = "re" }, .{ .degree = 3, .letter = "E", .solfege = "mi" }, .{ .degree = 4, .letter = "F", .solfege = "fa" }, .{ .degree = 5, .letter = "G", .solfege = "sol" }, .{ .degree = 6, .letter = "A", .solfege = "la" }, .{ .degree = 7, .letter = "B", .solfege = "si" }, }; /// The degree `steps` scale steps above `degree`, within one octave: 6 and 2 steps up is 1. fn degreeAbove(degree: u8, steps: u8) u8 { return (degree - 1 + steps) % 7 + 1; } /// What a triad of the major scale is: major (a major third, then a minor third above it), minor (a minor third, then /// a major third) or diminished (two minor thirds, its fifth a semitone short of a perfect fifth). In a major scale the /// triads on degrees 1, 4 and 5 are major, on 2, 3 and 6 minor, and on 7 diminished. const ChordQuality = enum { major, minor, diminished }; /// A chord of the scale: the degree of its root, its quality, and its name - a Roman numeral, upper case for a major /// triad and lower case for a minor one; the diminished triad's numeral carries a degree sign. const ScaleChord = struct { root_degree: u8, quality: ChordQuality, name: []const u8, /// The chord's three notes, as degrees: its root, the third above it, the fifth above it - each two scale steps /// above the one before, wrapping past 7 back to 1. fn degrees(chord: ScaleChord) [3]u8 { const root: u8 = chord.root_degree; return .{ root, degreeAbove(root, 2), degreeAbove(root, 4) }; } /// Whether the chord is drawn on the minor side: inside the circle, as a circle. fn isMinorSide(chord: ScaleChord) bool { return chord.quality != .major; } }; /// The seven chords of C major, by the degree of their root. const scale_chords = [7]ScaleChord{ .{ .root_degree = 1, .quality = .major, .name = "I" }, .{ .root_degree = 2, .quality = .minor, .name = "ii" }, .{ .root_degree = 3, .quality = .minor, .name = "iii" }, .{ .root_degree = 4, .quality = .major, .name = "IV" }, .{ .root_degree = 5, .quality = .major, .name = "V" }, .{ .root_degree = 6, .quality = .minor, .name = "vi" }, .{ .root_degree = 7, .quality = .diminished, .name = "vii\u{00b0}" }, }; /// The semitones from C up to each degree of C major: whole, whole, half, whole, whole, whole steps - the major scale's /// pattern, whose last half step returns to C an octave up. const semitones_above_tonic = [7]u8{ 0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 11 }; /// The MIDI key the scale's tonic plays at: 60, middle C. A Shepard note ignores the octave - only the key's pitch /// class chooses its partials - but the keys stay those of one real octave, so that another instrument plays them as /// they are. const tonic_key: u8 = 60; /// The MIDI key of a degree. fn keyOfDegree(degree: u8) u8 { return tonic_key + semitones_above_tonic[degree - 1]; } /// How hard every note is struck: half the instrument's full level, so that a chord of three stays clear of clipping. const note_velocity: f32 = 0.5; /// The keys that play each degree while held: the top row's digits and the keypad's. const digit_keys = [7]z.KeyboardKey{ .one, .two, .three, .four, .five, .six, .seven }; const keypad_keys = [7]z.KeyboardKey{ .kp_1, .kp_2, .kp_3, .kp_4, .kp_5, .kp_6, .kp_7 }; /// Where a degree sits on the circle of thirds, counted clockwise from the top: 0 for 1, then 1 for 3, 2 for 5, 3 for /// 7, 4 for 2, 5 for 4, 6 for 6. Walking the circle adds two degrees a place, so the place of a degree undoes that /// walk: multiplying by 4 undoes multiplying by 2, since 2 x 4 = 8, which is 1 more than a whole circle of 7. fn circlePlaceOfDegree(degree: u8) u8 { return (4 * (degree - 1)) % 7; } comptime { // The circle of thirds as the drawing needs it, checked when compiling: every degree has a place of its own, and // every chord is three neighbours - its third one place clockwise of its root, its fifth two places. var is_place_taken: [7]bool = @splat(false); for (scale_notes) |note| { const place: u8 = circlePlaceOfDegree(note.degree); if (is_place_taken[place]) { @compileError("two degrees share a place on the circle of thirds"); } is_place_taken[place] = true; } for (scale_chords) |chord| { const chord_degrees: [3]u8 = chord.degrees(); const root_place: u8 = circlePlaceOfDegree(chord_degrees[0]); const is_third_next: bool = circlePlaceOfDegree(chord_degrees[1]) == (root_place + 1) % 7; const is_fifth_after: bool = circlePlaceOfDegree(chord_degrees[2]) == (root_place + 2) % 7; if (!is_third_next or !is_fifth_after) { @compileError("a chord's notes are not three neighbours on the circle of thirds"); } } } // ---- The layout ---- /// The shape a note or a chord is drawn as: a square on the major side of the scale - the chords I, IV and V, and the /// notes 1, 4 and 5, whose own chords they are - and a circle on the minor side: ii, iii, vi and vii, and the notes 2, /// 3, 6 and 7. const Shape = enum { square, circle }; fn shapeOfChord(chord: ScaleChord) Shape { return if (chord.isMinorSide()) .circle else .square; } fn shapeOfDegree(degree: u8) Shape { return shapeOfChord(scale_chords[degree - 1]); } /// A shape and its size, in size units: the half-side of a square or the radius of a circle. A note is one unit; a /// chord, two - twice a note's size, as the larger target, since it plays three notes - except the diminished chord, /// vii, the scale's least used, at one and a half. const ShapedSize = struct { shape: Shape, size_in_units: f32, }; const note_size_in_units: f32 = 1; const chord_size_in_units: f32 = 2; const diminished_chord_size_in_units: f32 = 1.5; fn chordSizeInUnits(chord: ScaleChord) f32 { return if (chord.quality == .diminished) diminished_chord_size_in_units else chord_size_in_units; } fn shapedSizeOfChord(chord: ScaleChord) ShapedSize { return .{ .shape = shapeOfChord(chord), .size_in_units = chordSizeInUnits(chord) }; } /// How far `point` is from a shape centred at `centre`, of half-size `half_size`: 0 inside it, else the distance to /// its nearest edge, or corner. fn distanceToShape(point: Vec2, centre: Vec2, shape: Shape, half_size: f32) f32 { const offset: Vec2 = point - centre; switch (shape) { .circle => return @max(length(offset) - half_size, 0), .square => { const outside: Vec2 = @max(@abs(offset) - splat2(half_size), splat2(0)); return length(outside); }, } } /// The point where a ray from a shape's centre toward `target` leaves the shape: at its radius for a circle; for a /// square, where the ray meets the nearer of its vertical and horizontal edges - at the fraction of the way to the /// target that reaches the first of them. fn shapeEdgeToward(centre: Vec2, shape: Shape, half_size: f32, target: Vec2) Vec2 { const offset: Vec2 = target - centre; const offset_length: f32 = length(offset); if (offset_length == 0) { return centre; } switch (shape) { .circle => return centre + offset * splat2(half_size / offset_length), .square => { const fraction_to_side: f32 = if (offset[0] == 0) 1 else half_size / @abs(offset[0]); const fraction_to_top: f32 = if (offset[1] == 0) 1 else half_size / @abs(offset[1]); const fraction: f32 = @min(fraction_to_side, fraction_to_top, 1); return centre + offset * splat2(fraction); }, } } /// The largest size unit `u` at which two shapes, their centres `offset` apart, are at least `clearance` units apart: /// /// two circles u <= distance / (a + b + c) a, b their sizes in units, c the clearance /// two squares u <= max(|dx|, |dy|) / (a + b + c) apart in x or in y is enough /// a circle and the square's nearest point at least (a + c) u from the circle's centre /// a square /// /// For the last, as `u` grows the square grows toward the circle while the distance needed grows too, so there is a /// single largest `u`, found by halving an interval that holds it - from 0 to the distance between the centres - 24 /// times, to within a 16-millionth of that distance. fn largestUnitApart( offset: Vec2, first: ShapedSize, second: ShapedSize, clearance: f32, ) f32 { const apart: Vec2 = @abs(offset); const sizes_and_clearance: f32 = first.size_in_units + second.size_in_units + clearance; if (first.shape == .circle and second.shape == .circle) { return length(apart) / sizes_and_clearance; } if (first.shape == .square and second.shape == .square) { return @max(apart[0], apart[1]) / sizes_and_clearance; } const circle: ShapedSize = if (first.shape == .circle) first else second; const square: ShapedSize = if (first.shape == .square) first else second; var clear_unit: f32 = 0; var touching_unit: f32 = length(apart); for (0..24) |_| { const trial_unit: f32 = (clear_unit + touching_unit) / 2; const half_square: Vec2 = @splat(square.size_in_units * trial_unit); const outside_square: Vec2 = @max(apart - half_square, splat2(0)); const is_clear: bool = length(outside_square) >= (circle.size_in_units + clearance) * trial_unit; if (is_clear) { clear_unit = trial_unit; } else { touching_unit = trial_unit; } } return clear_unit; } /// Where everything is drawn, worked out from the window's size each frame so that the drawing fills the window, /// whatever its shape. /// /// The notes sit on an ellipse rather than a circle - as wide as the window allows and as tall - so that on a phone /// held upright the notes spread down the whole screen, and on one held sideways across it. The chords sit on two more /// ellipses of the same shape, one outside for the major chords and one inside for the others, each chord at the /// angle of its third. /// /// The sizes follow from those places. A note is `u` in size and a chord `2 u` (`ShapedSize`), and `u` is the /// largest size at which no two of the fourteen come too near each other (`largestSizeUnit`). Since the figure must /// also fit the window, and its size is what is being found, the two are settled together: the figure is stretched /// to the window at the sizes found (`fitToRoom`), `u` is found again for the new places, and so on - a few rounds, /// each changing less than the one before. /// /// The figure adapts to the screen's shape in four ways, and the layout is worked out for every combination, the one /// with the largest notes drawn (`ofWindow`): /// /// the figure's turn 1 at the top, or a quarter turn round with 1 at the right: with 1 at the top the chords /// ii and iii sit side by side, which a narrow screen squeezes /// the button's corner a page's fullscreen button covers the window's bottom right corner, which the figure /// leaves free: as a strip along the right edge, or one along the bottom /// the inner chords their ellipse's size, as a fraction of the notes': nearer the centre leaves more room /// between them and their notes, nearer the notes more room among themselves /// the outer chords their ellipse's size: further out leaves more room between them and their notes, and /// less for the figure /// /// Since it tries dozens of layouts, the app keeps the one chosen until the window's size changes (`layoutOf`). const Layout = struct { centre: Vec2, /// The half-width and the half-height of the ellipse the notes sit on. note_ellipse_radii: Vec2, /// Where place 0 - the degree 1 - sits, in turns clockwise from the top: 0, or a quarter turn. rotation_turns: f32, /// The chords' ellipses, as multiples of the notes': the major chords' outside, the others' inside. outer_chord_scale: f32, inner_chord_scale: f32, /// A note's half-size: the half-side of its square, or its circle's radius. A chord's is twice it. size_unit: f32, /// The sizes of the chords' ellipses `ofWindow` tries, as multiples of the notes'. const outer_chord_scales = [_]f32{ 1.5, 1.62, 1.75 }; const inner_chord_scales = [_]f32{ 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7 }; /// The height of the line of text at the top, and the gap kept along the window's edges. const header_height: f32 = 26; const margin: f32 = 6; /// The corner a page's fullscreen button covers: the button's 52 pixels and its 10 from the window's edges. const fullscreen_button_reach: f32 = 62; /// The rounds `settled` takes to settle the places and the sizes together. const settling_rounds: usize = 5; fn ofWindow(f: *z.Frame) Layout { const width: f32 = f.window.widthf(); const height: f32 = f.window.heightf(); const whole_room: z.Rectangle = .{ .x = margin, .y = header_height + margin, .width = width - 2 * margin, .height = height - header_height - 2 * margin, }; // The fullscreen button's corner left free along the right edge, or along the bottom. var room_beside_button: z.Rectangle = whole_room; room_beside_button.width -= fullscreen_button_reach - margin; var room_above_button: z.Rectangle = whole_room; room_above_button.height -= fullscreen_button_reach - margin; const rooms = [2]z.Rectangle{ room_beside_button, room_above_button }; const rotations = [2]f32{ 0, 0.25 }; var best: ?Layout = null; for (rooms) |room| { for (rotations) |rotation_turns| { for (outer_chord_scales) |outer_chord_scale| { for (inner_chord_scales) |inner_chord_scale| { const scales: ChordScales = .{ .outer = outer_chord_scale, .inner = inner_chord_scale }; const candidate: Layout = settled(room, rotation_turns, scales); const best_size_unit: f32 = if (best) |best_so_far| best_so_far.size_unit else -1; const is_better: bool = candidate.size_unit > best_size_unit; if (is_better) { best = candidate; } } } } } return best.?; } /// The sizes of the chords' two ellipses, as multiples of the notes'. const ChordScales = struct { outer: f32, inner: f32, }; /// The layout with the figure turned by `rotation_turns` and its chords' ellipses at `scales`, its places and its /// sizes settled together in `room`. fn settled(room: z.Rectangle, rotation_turns: f32, scales: ChordScales) Layout { // First guess: no size at all, and the figure as large as the room. var layout: Layout = .{ .centre = .{ room.x + room.width / 2, room.y + room.height / 2 }, .note_ellipse_radii = .{ room.width, room.height }, .rotation_turns = rotation_turns, .outer_chord_scale = scales.outer, .inner_chord_scale = scales.inner, .size_unit = 0, }; layout.fitToRoom(room); for (0..settling_rounds) |_| { layout.size_unit = layout.largestSizeUnit(); layout.fitToRoom(room); } return layout; } fn noteHalfSize(layout: Layout) f32 { return note_size_in_units * layout.size_unit; } fn chordHalfSize(layout: Layout, chord: ScaleChord) f32 { return chordSizeInUnits(chord) * layout.size_unit; } /// The fourteen targets: seven notes, then seven chords. const target_count: usize = 14; /// Stretches the figure to fill `room`, at the sizes it has now: on each axis, the ellipses' radius and the /// figure's centre such that the figure's outermost note or chord touches the room's edges on both sides /// (`fitAxis`). fn fitToRoom(layout: *Layout, room: z.Rectangle) void { var place_offsets: [target_count]Vec2 = undefined; var half_sizes: [target_count]f32 = undefined; for (scale_notes, 0..) |note, note_index| { place_offsets[note_index] = layout.noteCentre(note.degree) - layout.centre; half_sizes[note_index] = layout.noteHalfSize(); } for (scale_chords, 0..) |chord, chord_index| { place_offsets[7 + chord_index] = layout.chordCentre(chord) - layout.centre; half_sizes[7 + chord_index] = layout.chordHalfSize(chord); } // The places, as multiples of the radii now: what each axis's radius scales. var coefficients: [2][target_count]f32 = undefined; inline for (0..2) |axis| { for (0..target_count) |target_index| { const radius: f32 = layout.note_ellipse_radii[axis]; coefficients[axis][target_index] = place_offsets[target_index][axis] / radius; } } const fit_x: AxisFit = fitAxis(&coefficients[0], &half_sizes, room.width); const fit_y: AxisFit = fitAxis(&coefficients[1], &half_sizes, room.height); layout.note_ellipse_radii = .{ fit_x.radius, fit_y.radius }; layout.centre = .{ room.x + fit_x.centre_from_start, room.y + fit_y.centre_from_start }; } /// One axis of a fit: the ellipses' radius along it, and where the figure's centre falls, from the room's start. const AxisFit = struct { radius: f32, centre_from_start: f32, }; /// The largest radius at which targets placed at `coefficients x radius` from the centre, each `half_sizes` to /// either side, span no more than `room_length`, and the centre that puts that span in the middle of the room. /// The span only grows with the radius, so the largest is found by halving an interval that holds it, 32 times. fn fitAxis( coefficients: *const [target_count]f32, half_sizes: *const [target_count]f32, room_length: f32, ) AxisFit { var fitting_radius: f32 = 0; var too_large_radius: f32 = 4 * room_length; for (0..32) |_| { const trial_radius: f32 = (fitting_radius + too_large_radius) / 2; const trial_span: Span = spanAt(coefficients, half_sizes, trial_radius); if (trial_span.high - trial_span.low <= room_length) { fitting_radius = trial_radius; } else { too_large_radius = trial_radius; } } const span: Span = spanAt(coefficients, half_sizes, fitting_radius); // The span's middle at the room's middle. return .{ .radius = fitting_radius, .centre_from_start = room_length / 2 - (span.low + span.high) / 2 }; } /// Where the figure reaches along one axis, measured from its centre: its lowest and its highest points. const Span = struct { low: f32, high: f32, }; fn spanAt( coefficients: *const [target_count]f32, half_sizes: *const [target_count]f32, radius: f32, ) Span { var span: Span = .{ .low = inf(f32), .high = -inf(f32) }; for (coefficients, half_sizes) |coefficient, half_size| { const centre_offset: f32 = coefficient * radius; span.low = @min(span.low, centre_offset - half_size); span.high = @max(span.high, centre_offset + half_size); } return span; } /// The clear space kept between two targets, in size units: between any two, and - wider, so that the lines /// between them have room to show their shapes - between a chord and its own three notes. const clearance_in_units: f32 = 0.3; const own_note_clearance_in_units: f32 = 0.55; /// The largest size unit at which none of the fourteen targets comes nearer another than its clearance, at the /// places the ellipses give them now: the smallest of the limits every pair sets (`largestUnitApart`). fn largestSizeUnit(layout: Layout) f32 { var size_unit: f32 = inf(f32); for (scale_notes, 0..) |note, note_index| { const note_centre: Vec2 = layout.noteCentre(note.degree); const note_shape: ShapedSize = .{ .shape = shapeOfDegree(note.degree), .size_in_units = note_size_in_units, }; for (scale_notes[note_index + 1 ..]) |other_note| { const other_shape: ShapedSize = .{ .shape = shapeOfDegree(other_note.degree), .size_in_units = note_size_in_units, }; const offset: Vec2 = layout.noteCentre(other_note.degree) - note_centre; size_unit = @min(size_unit, largestUnitApart(offset, note_shape, other_shape, clearance_in_units)); } for (scale_chords) |chord| { const is_own_note: bool = indexOfScalar(u8, &chord.degrees(), note.degree) != null; const clearance: f32 = if (is_own_note) own_note_clearance_in_units else clearance_in_units; const chord_shape: ShapedSize = shapedSizeOfChord(chord); const offset: Vec2 = layout.chordCentre(chord) - note_centre; size_unit = @min(size_unit, largestUnitApart(offset, note_shape, chord_shape, clearance)); } } for (scale_chords, 0..) |chord, chord_index| { const chord_centre: Vec2 = layout.chordCentre(chord); const chord_shape: ShapedSize = shapedSizeOfChord(chord); for (scale_chords[chord_index + 1 ..]) |other_chord| { const other_shape: ShapedSize = shapedSizeOfChord(other_chord); const offset: Vec2 = layout.chordCentre(other_chord) - chord_centre; size_unit = @min(size_unit, largestUnitApart(offset, chord_shape, other_shape, clearance_in_units)); } } return size_unit; } /// The point at place `circle_place` of 7, clockwise from the figure's top, on the notes' ellipse scaled by /// `scale`. Angles are in turns: place `k` is `k / 7` of a turn round from the figure's rotation. The screen's y /// grows downward, so the top is -y. fn pointAtPlace(layout: Layout, circle_place: u8, scale: f32) Vec2 { const angle_turns: f32 = layout.rotation_turns + float(circle_place) / 7; const direction: Vec2 = .{ sinTurns(angle_turns), -cosTurns(angle_turns) }; const radii: Vec2 = layout.note_ellipse_radii * splat2(scale); return layout.centre + direction * radii; } fn noteCentre(layout: Layout, degree: u8) Vec2 { return layout.pointAtPlace(circlePlaceOfDegree(degree), 1); } /// A chord's centre: at the place of its third, on the outer ellipse for a major chord, the inner for the others. fn chordCentre(layout: Layout, chord: ScaleChord) Vec2 { const third_degree: u8 = chord.degrees()[1]; const scale: f32 = if (chord.isMinorSide()) layout.inner_chord_scale else layout.outer_chord_scale; return layout.pointAtPlace(circlePlaceOfDegree(third_degree), scale); } }; // ---- Drawing ---- /// What the pointer presses: a note, by its degree, or a chord, by its index in `scale_chords`. const PointerTarget = union(enum) { note: u8, chord: u8, }; /// A pointer holding a target: a finger, by the identifier the platform gives it for as long as it touches - the /// same from frame to frame, wherever it moves - or the mouse. const PointerHold = struct { pointer_id: i32, target: PointerTarget, }; /// The most pointers held at once: the ten touches the engine tracks, and the mouse. const most_pointers: usize = 11; /// The mouse's identifier among the pointers: one no touch is given, touches being numbered up from 0. const mouse_pointer_id: i32 = -1; /// A pointer down this frame: its identifier and where it is. const PointerNow = struct { pointer_id: i32, position: Vec2, }; const State = struct { font: z.Font, /// For each degree, how many things hold its note down: its key, each finger on the note, each finger on a chord /// that contains it.
